template_name: Extract and Apply a Precedential Principle
description: Derive the legally operative principle from an earlier authority and test whether that principle governs the present issue, rather than treating factual resemblance or a broad case label as sufficient.
application_scenario: Use when a prior decision is invoked for a proposition and the present dispute requires deciding how far that proposition extends.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise issue for which the earlier authority is cited.
Extract the rule or principle necessary to the earlier decision and separate it from fact-specific observations.
List the legally material facts and statutory or contractual setting of the earlier decision.
Compare those features with the present dispute at the same level of abstraction.
Apply the principle only to the extent justified by the shared material features and record any limits on its scope.
example_application: A prior property decision interprets a restriction on use. The analysis isolates the interpretation principle, compares the governing instrument and type of use in the present dispute, and carries over only the proposition that remains valid across both settings.

template_name: Distinguish an Authority by a Material Difference
description: Determine whether a cited authority should be given reduced weight because a factual, procedural, statutory, or remedial difference changes the reason the earlier rule operated.
application_scenario: Use when two disputes appear similar at a surface level but differ in a feature that may alter the governing analysis.
reasoning_flow: State the proposition for which the authority is relied upon.
Identify the feature that was essential to the earlier court's reasoning.
Locate the corresponding feature in the present dispute.
Assess whether the difference affects the rule's rationale, statutory setting, burden, or available remedy.
Explain which parts of the authority remain persuasive and which parts do not transfer.
example_application: An earlier tenancy case concerned an uninterrupted statutory status, while the present dispute includes a later transaction or procedural step. The analysis asks whether that intervening feature changes the rationale of the earlier decision rather than treating both matters as identical.

template_name: Interpret a Contested Term Through Text, Context, and Purpose
description: Resolve the scope of a disputed statutory, contractual, or instrument-based term by integrating its ordinary or defined meaning, surrounding provisions, regulatory purpose, and treatment in analogous authorities or enactments.
application_scenario: Use when liability, entitlement, classification, or jurisdiction turns on whether a person, object, act, or alteration falls within a disputed term.
reasoning_flow: Identify the exact term and the legal consequence attached to its inclusion or exclusion.
Read any express definition together with the immediate provision and the wider scheme.
Test candidate meanings against the instrument's evident purpose and internal coherence.
Consult analogous provisions and prior interpretations while checking for differences in wording and purpose.
Select the meaning that best reconciles text, context, purpose, and any applicable precedent.
example_application: A regulatory provision lists a category of animals or building works. The analysis compares the listed language, the purpose of the scheme, related enactments, and earlier interpretations before determining whether the disputed item belongs to the category.

template_name: Resolve Rights Across Amendments, Transfers, and Procedural Changes
description: Determine whether an existing statutory or contractual right continues, revives, transfers, or is displaced after an amendment, notice, withdrawal, assignment, or change of legal actor.
application_scenario: Use when a party's present status depends on the legal effect of an earlier step followed by a later change in law, ownership, notice, or procedure.
reasoning_flow: Construct the sequence of legally significant events without relying on immaterial chronology.
Identify the right or status created, altered, or terminated at each step.
Read the governing provisions for express transitional, revival, adoption, or successor rules.
Compare analogous authorities involving the same type of intervening event.
Determine the present legal status by linking each event to its legal effect and avoiding assumptions of automatic continuity or revival.
example_application: A protected occupancy is followed by a statutory notice, a later withdrawal, and a change of landlord. The analysis traces whether protection ended, revived, or could be adopted by the successor under the governing scheme.

template_name: Determine Property Rights from the Instrument and Chain of Title
description: Establish the existence and extent of a property interest by reading the governing deed or assignment, tracing later transfers, and reconciling registration with statutory and equitable rules.
application_scenario: Use when ownership, exclusive use, common-part status, co-ownership shares, or retained rights are disputed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the specific physical area or proprietary interest in dispute.
Read the original grant, deed, assignment, or management instrument for the rights expressly created or reserved.
Trace whether later instruments could validly transfer the asserted interest.
Check registration, statutory vesting, common-part rules, and any equitable ownership claim.
Resolve inconsistencies by distinguishing legal title, beneficial interest, management responsibility, and mere use or access.
example_application: Successive assignments describe an exclusive right over part of a building, while the governing deed allocates maintenance and access collectively. The analysis tests whether the original owner retained a transferable interest and whether later instruments conveyed more than was legally available.

template_name: Attribute Property-Related Responsibility Through Control and Duty
description: Identify the person or body legally responsible for a property-related hazard or loss by connecting the source location, actual or legal control, maintenance obligations, and causal contribution.
application_scenario: Use when harm is alleged to arise from a building area, stored goods, structural condition, or object whose source and responsible controller are disputed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the alleged source of the hazard or damaging event.
Classify the relevant area or object as private, common, retained, occupied, or otherwise controlled.
Determine who had the legal duty and practical ability to inspect, maintain, remove, or secure it.
Evaluate evidence connecting the condition or conduct to the loss, including alternative sources.
Compare analogous cases only after aligning the type of control, duty, and causal mechanism.
example_application: An object or hazardous condition associated with a multi-unit building causes injury or damage. The analysis first locates its probable source, then maps that source to control and maintenance duties before considering whether an earlier building-liability authority is closely analogous.

template_name: Separate Statutory Entitlement from Remedial Discretion
description: Analyze a requested remedy in two stages: first determine whether the legal threshold or jurisdictional conditions are met, then evaluate whether discretion should be exercised in light of hardship, fairness, proportionality, safeguards, and alternatives.
application_scenario: Use for possession, sale, injunction, winding-up, wardship, compulsory process, or other remedies that are legally available only after threshold conditions and a discretionary assessment.
reasoning_flow: Identify every mandatory precondition for the court's power to act.
Match the material facts to each precondition and keep threshold findings separate from discretionary considerations.
Identify the interests likely to be affected and the nature of any hardship, prejudice, or procedural unfairness.
Assess safeguards, undertakings, narrower measures, and practical alternatives.
Use analogous decisions to calibrate the discretion while preserving differences in statutory purpose and factual severity.
example_application: An applicant satisfies an ownership or procedural threshold for a property remedy, but another occupier alleges severe hardship. The analysis verifies the threshold first and then separately weighs hardship, alternatives, and protective conditions.

template_name: Assess Interim Financial Provision from Needs and Resources
description: Set an interim financial framework by comparing reasonable current needs with available resources, prior living arrangements, child-related expenses, earning capacity, and the reliability of financial disclosure.
application_scenario: Use when temporary maintenance or related family provision must be assessed before final financial issues are resolved.
reasoning_flow: Identify the interim period, persons needing provision, and categories of claimed expenditure.
Separate reasonable recurring needs from capital, duplicated, speculative, or final-distribution items.
Assess income, assets, liabilities, earning capacity, housing circumstances, and existing contributions on both sides.
Account for the prior standard of living without converting an interim assessment into a final division of resources.
Address incomplete disclosure through cautious inference and cross-check the proposed provision against affordability and the child's or dependent's immediate welfare.
example_application: One spouse seeks temporary housing and living expenses for a child while the other disputes both the budget and available income. The analysis reviews the actual expense categories, historical living pattern, current resources, and gaps in disclosure to construct a workable interim provision.

template_name: Value Property Through Comparable Evidence and Legal Adjustments
description: Estimate property value or compensation by selecting genuinely comparable evidence and making transparent adjustments for physical features, occupation, timing, planning controls, statutory assumptions, and the effect of the relevant scheme.
application_scenario: Use when a tribunal must determine open-market value, compensation for interference or resumption, or another property-based monetary measure.
reasoning_flow: Define the valuation date, legal basis, and any mandatory statutory assumptions.
Identify the property's legally and economically relevant characteristics.
Select transactions or rental evidence with the closest location, use, condition, tenure, and timing.
Adjust for material differences and explain the direction and basis of each adjustment.
Separate market effects that properly attach to the property from effects that the governing compensation rule requires to be ignored or treated specially.
Cross-check the result against alternative valuation methods and the evidential reliability of the inputs.
example_application: A resumed or impaired property lies within a redevelopment area. The analysis selects nearby transactions, adjusts for size, use, condition, and occupation, and then applies the statutory rule governing whether scheme-related effects enter the valuation.

template_name: Define Proportionate Discovery by Relevance and Search Burden
description: Determine the proper scope and method of discovery by linking requested material to pleaded issues, evaluating the adequacy of prior searches, and balancing likely evidential value against cost, volume, duplication, and technological feasibility.
application_scenario: Use for specific discovery, challenges to discovery compliance, or proposed technology-assisted review and electronic search protocols.
reasoning_flow: Map each requested category to a pleaded issue or a reasonably identifiable evidential question.
Define the applicable relevance standard and exclude requests based only on speculation or general curiosity.
Review preservation, custodians, data sources, search terms, sampling, and prior production to identify concrete gaps.
Estimate the burden and likely yield of additional manual or technology-assisted searching.
Design a staged, testable, and auditable protocol using sampling, validation, or targeted production where appropriate.
Compare procedural authorities with attention to differences in data volume, case complexity, and the governing discovery standard.
example_application: A party seeks additional records from a very large electronic collection and alleges that the existing search was too narrow. The analysis connects each category to an issue, examines the search methodology, and considers a validated technological protocol rather than assuming that maximum collection is necessary.
